verdict: A thin day: mostly arXiv paper noise, Luma AI SEO-prompt spam, and studio PR pieces, with one genuine gaussian-splatting production item and a couple of items worth a glance for licence and legal reasons.

stories.headline: IBC 2026 show floor report covers Gaussian splatting and scene-aware camera tracking
stories.body: postPerspective's IBC 2026 walkaround notes splatting and synchronized scene-aware camera tools were a recurring theme among exhibitors this year, alongside broader optimism despite a down production market. No specific vendor names or product details are given in this summary, so treat as a trend signal rather than a tool announcement worth acting on immediately.
stories.why: Signals gaussian splatting is moving from research demos toward broadcast/production tooling vendors are actively building.

stories.headline: A24's V/H/S: SCP spinoff reportedly made without contacting SCP Foundation's creators
stories.body: 80 Level reports A24 never contacted the original authors of the collaboratively-written SCP Foundation universe before producing a film based on it, and that a licensing arrangement limits how much the studio can profit from the project. Details on the underlying rights structure (SCP content is CC-BY-SA licensed by its community) are not fully spelled out in the source.
stories.why: A live example of how open-licence fan-created IP creates ambiguous rights exposure for studios adapting it.
